en.text: Amaranthus caudatus is an Andean species of annual flowering plant. It goes by common names such as love-lies-bleeding, pendant amaranth, tassel flower, velvet flower, and foxtail amaranth. In South America, it is known as kiwicha.

es.text: Amaranthus caudatus, comúnmente llamada quihuicha en Perú y Bolivia, amaranto en México y Centroamérica, o moco de pavo en España, es una planta de la familia de las amarantáceas de rápido crecimiento, con hojas, tallos y flores morados, rojos y dorados. Es considerada una planta nutracéutica y sus semillas un alimento funcional.

fr.text: L'amarante queue-de-renard ou amarante caudée est une espèce de plante herbacée de la famille des Amaranthacées. Elle atteint une hauteur d'un mètre. Elle est aussi nommée Kiwicha, de son nom en langue quechua au Pérou où elle est cultivée à des fins alimentaires.

pt.text: Amaranthus caudatus (Jimboa), também conhecida como caruru, é uma espécie de planta com flor pertencente à família Amaranthaceae.

en.heading: Cultivation
en.text:
Despite the fact that A. caudatus had been a well-adapted staple in the Andean region for millennia and had offered substantial nutritional advantages to the native people, when the Spanish came in the 1500s, they replaced A. caudatus cultivations with wheat and barley. However, because of its great nutritional content, A. caudatus is regaining popularity and returning to compete with modern crops. Although A. caudatus is seldom recognized outside of the Andes, significant plantings have been observed in Mexico, China, Nepal, India and Kenya.
In most parts of its habitat, A. caudatus can easily grow between 1 and 2.5 m (3+1⁄2 and 8 ft) and grows best in full sun within 4–6 months. However, in some highland regions it can take up to 10 months. It is a summer annual C4 plant. It grows from Ecuador to northern Argentina mostly in mild areas or in the valleys of the Andes. Despite its geographical adaptability, it is a short-day plant and needs adequate moisture. Cultivation can occur at up to 3,100 m (10,200 ft) and once established it is drought tolerant and can handle both wet and dry conditions. If the cultivation takes place in subtropical climates, it can be harvested up to two times. Loam and loam-sandy soils with lots of organic matter and good drainage are best. Clay soils are not recommended for A. caudatus. In addition, the pH must be between 6–7, although the plant can still grow at a pH of up to 8.5.
The crop is planted by transfer, with the help of seedlings in fields or by direct drilling at the beginning of the rainy season. They are cut at a height of 10 to 55 cm (4 to 21+1⁄2 in) and the cultivation practices are similar to those of corn: ear emergence, two-stage fertilization and weed control.

fr.heading: Horticulture
fr.text: Elle peut être semée à l'intérieur dès le mois de mars ou directement en terre en mai.
